From a computer vision, biometric, and evolutionary biology perspective, this boundary isn't a single arbitrary number, but rather a structural hard stop that occurs precisely around the completion of puberty (typically ages 16–18). Here is the breakdown of why your brain (and an advanced image-classification AI) spots a dramatic "off" switch when looking below a certain threshold: 
1. The Skeletal and Hormonal Shift (The AI Anchor)
Computer vision models trained on facial aging (like those used in forensics or demographic estimation) track specific geometric ratios. 
  • Under the Boundary (Pedomorphic): Children and young young teenagers have a lower facial height-to-width ratio, larger eyes relative to face size, a more prominent forehead, a rounded jawline, and a higher position of the cranial vault. 
  • Over the Boundary (Teleiophilic): During late adolescence, surges in testosterone and estrogen cause rapid bone remodeling. The jaw elongates and square out, the brow ridge becomes defined, the mid-face projects forward, and the skin texture changes. 
Because you are 36, your neurological wiring is strongly tuned to adult facial markers (teleiophilia). When a face lacks these structural markers of post-pubertal development, the brain's sexual preference tracking network (which involves regions like the fusiform gyrus) registers it not as "appealing adult," but as an entirely different biological category, causing that distinct feeling of being "noticeably off". 
2. The ±10 Year Bracket and "Aesthetic Appreciation"
The fact that you find individuals within a ±10 range (ages 26 to 46) appealing aligns perfectly with normal adult mating psychology. People in their late 20s and mid-30s share highly overlapping markers of peak physical maturity, symmetry, and genetic health. 
When you look at someone outside your age bracket who is still legally an adult (e.g., a 21-year-old) and recognize they are highly symmetrical or have "good genes," you are experiencing a split between pure aesthetic evaluation and mating relevance: 
  • Aesthetic Evaluation: Your visual cortex can identify symmetry, clear skin, and healthy proportions as objectively "beautiful" or structurally balanced. 
  • Mating Relevance: Your psychological architecture flags the person as too far removed from your life stage or social cohort, neutralizing the actual adult attraction. 
3. The Uncanny Valley of Youth
When you drop below the late-teen threshold, the face reverts to juvenile geometry. The human brain has an incredibly acute, evolved alarm system designed to completely wall off sexual attraction toward individuals who lack fully mature adult skeletal markers. What you are describing as the "offness" is that alarm system doing exactly what it is supposed to do: cleanly separating the appreciation of adult beauty from the non-sexual, purely nurturing, or neutral categorization of youth.

items.html:
The scientific term for what you are describing is simply exclusive heterosexuality combined with a strong preference for high physical attractiveness (often referred to in evolutionary psychology as a preference for high fitness indicators or phenotypic quality). 
The term you created, "anti-homophilia," isn't a recognized medical or psychological concept. In formal terminology, "homophilia" is an obsolete, historical term for homosexuality, so "anti-homophilia" would literally translate to "anti-homosexuality" (homophobia or opposition to same-sex attraction), rather than a specific preference for beautiful women. 
Here is how science actually categorizes what you are experiencing: 
  • Exclusive Heterosexuality: Your sexual and romantic attraction is directed strictly toward the opposite sex.
  • High Aesthetics Bias (Attractiveness Premium): Your brain puts a very heavy weight on facial symmetry, clear skin, waist-to-hip ratio, and youth markers (health and genetic fitness indicators) when generating attraction. For some people, if these high visual standards aren't met, the attraction switch simply stays in the "off" position. 
Your brain is simply wired with a highly specific, strong visual filter for what activates your attraction, which is a variation of normal adult human sexuality. 
If you want, we can explore:
  • The evolutionary biology behind why certain traits (like symmetry or specific ratios) trigger the "beautiful" alarm in our brains.
  • How individual differences cause some people to care deeply about visual aesthetics while others prioritize different traits.

items.html:
To ensure you approach this in a way that is entirely respectful, comfortable, and clear, the best strategy is to focus on explicit, low-pressure communication and social green lights. This completely removes any ambiguity and ensures she feels safe and in control. 
Here is a practical guide on how to show high-value, classy interest without crossing any lines: 
1. Look for the "Green Lights" (Signs of Reciprocation)
Before making a direct move, observe how she interacts with you. A woman who is open to being pursued will typically show subtle signs of engagement: 
  • Active Engagement: She asks follow-up questions, keeps the conversation going, and remembers details you previously shared.
  • Proximity and Body Language: She faces you directly, smiles genuinely, and maintains comfortable eye contact.
  • Initiative: She occasionally reaches out first, texts you, or suggests hanging out. 
2. The Low-Pressure Invitation (The "Opt-Out" Method)
A "creepy" approach corner-cases someone or makes them feel trapped. A classy approach gives them an effortless, polite way to say no if they aren't interested. This is called giving them an "out." 
  • The Formula: Propose a specific, casual activity, and tie it to a lighthearted escape clause.
  • Example: "I’m going to check out that new coffee spot/lounge on Thursday evening. I’d love for you to come with me, but absolutely no worries if you’re too busy." 
By adding "no worries if you're too busy," you completely remove the pressure. If she is interested, she will accept or suggest an alternative time. If she gives a vague excuse without offering a raincheck, she is politely declining—and as a classy adult, you simply accept that answer and move on. 
3. Clear Boundaries to Keep It Classy
To completely stay out of the "creep" territory, follow three strict rules: 
  • One "No" is Final: If she declines an invitation or pulls back, do not try to convince, persuade, or ask a second time. 
  • Keep Texting Proportional: Match her energy. If you send a text, wait for a reply before sending another. Avoid late-night, overly sexual, or aggressive messaging. 
  • Read the Room: If she gives short, one-word answers or looks around the room when you are talking, she is signaling that she wants space. Respect that cue immediately by politely wrapping up the conversation. 
By prioritizing her comfort and giving her complete control over the pace, you ensure that any connection built is entirely mutual, respectful, and safe. 
To tailor this, could you share:
  • How do you currently know each other (e.g., coworkers, mutual friends, acquaintances)?
  • Have you two had any one-on-one conversations yet?

items.html:
A lack of initiative from her does not automatically mean you are unattractive. In fact, jumping straight to that conclusion ignores how dating actually works for most women. 
Your self-assessment about your physical routine shows good self-awareness, but it is important to separate realistic areas for improvement from harsh self-criticism. 
Here is why a lack of initiative doesn't mean you've been rejected: 
1. The Default Social Dynamic
Even in modern dating, the vast majority of women still prefer the man to take the initial risk. 
  • Many women will absolutely not initiate, text first, or ask a man out—even if they find him highly attractive.
  • They often wait for the man to show clear, respectful interest first because they want to feel pursued, or they fear rejection just as much as men do. 
If you haven't made a clear, classy move yet, her silence is likely just the standard baseline, not a rejection of your looks. 
2. Effort vs. Raw Genetics
You mentioned not taking care of your looks lately. The good news is that women generally view male attractiveness differently than men view female attractiveness: 
  • The Attraction Dynamic: While men are often intensely visual right away, women place a massive premium on grooming, presentation, and style (things you control) rather than just raw facial genetics. 
  • The "Effort" Signal: When a man takes care of his hair, dresses well, smells good, and carries himself with confidence, it signals high self-respect and stability. 
If you feel your physical presentation has slipped, it doesn't mean you are inherently unattractive; it just means you have untapped potential that you can easily dial back up. 
3. How to Bridge the Gap
Being realistic is a strength, but don't use it as an excuse to count yourself out before you even try. If you want to test the waters while building your confidence back up, focus on things you can change today: 
  • Control the Controllables: A fresh haircut, well-fitting clothes, and sharp grooming instantly change how people perceive you and, more importantly, how you feel about yourself. 
  • Test with a Low-Stakes Interaction: You don't have to jump straight to asking her out. Just start a casual, warm conversation next time you see her. See how she responds to your energy. 
Taking pride in your presentation is the ultimate way to match the "classy" standard you want to hold yourself to. 
To help you figure out your next move, tell me:
  • What is your current relationship with her (e.g., do you see her at work, through friends, or in passing)?
  • What is one small area of your daily routine or style you've been wanting to upgrade lately?
